claims.claim: Credits are not charged at a flat rate per response.
claims.guide_evidence: Message credits are not consumed at a flat rate.

claims.claim: Lighter models can cost as little as 1 credit per response.
claims.guide_evidence: lighter models (for example smaller GPT variants) consume as little as 1 credit per response

claims.claim: Mid-tier models cost around 5 credits per response.
Heavier or multimodal models (transcription, text-to-speech, flagship chat) cost around 10 credits per response.
claims.guide_evidence: larger or multimodal models (audio transcription, text-to-speech, flagship chat models) around 10 credits per response

claims.claim: A shift toward a heavier model could on its own explain faster credit burn, even with no change in request volume.
claims.guide_evidence: A workspace that mostly uses a heavier model will exhaust its credit balance noticeably faster than the headline credit number suggests.

claims.claim: The app or its users may have been using a heavier model more often this week.
Checking the usage logs to see which model handled the most requests this week should confirm the cause.

sub_questions.question: Why did my credit balance drop faster this week when I didn't change how I use the app?

evaluation.rationale: The guide supports the explanation that credits vary by model, and so does the per-model credit breakdown. The answer offers this as a possible cause rather than a definite diagnosis, which is reasonable. The only problems are minor: it guesses the model mix changed, even though the customer says nothing changed, and it points to "usage logs" that the guide never mentions.
